newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest bourse reopens, most prices down.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest bourse reopens, most prices down.

text.p: Most Bucharest share prices sagged under heavy supply on Thursday, when the bourse reopened for trading after staying closed for three consecutive sessions to install a new software to improve trading and settlement.
"Orders have amassed during the two-week break, but they were mostly sell notes pulling prices down," one trader said.
Brokers said the new software had failed to give a boost to trading on Thursday, when turnover kept low at 62.2 million lei, close to a previous 50.1 million level.
"The new software allows brokers put together more orders being able to trade more shares at one time but for the time being this market is rather illiquid," said a broker.
The Bursa de Valori Bucuresti trades 13 stocks, of which only one is privately held.
"Buying interest was scant, with investors awaiting some 10 companies which applied for a listing to join the market," another broker said.
The exchange said on Thursday four companies had applied for a quotation, adding to another seven which previously asked for a listing. It did not say when they would join in trading.
It also said it would soon handle public offerings for 14 state companies, including the national travel operator ONT Carpati SA and the country's only newsprint maker Letea SA.
"Twenty-five potential newcomers is something to look forward to," a trader said.
Fertiliser maker Azomures SA dominated trading with 75 percent of turnover. It closed 500 lei weaker at 10,200.

The unofficial VAB-Index -- a value-weighted index of all listed stocks computed by Vanguard SA securities -- fell 3.5 percent from the previous session to 311.4 points. The other independent index -- the BIG -- was not available on Thursday.
